steps.say: Milk discharge with missed periods points below the brain, not at the breast. A tiny pituitary lump explains both at once.
steps.tx: **Prolactinoma** (milk hormone lump) is the commonest functional pituitary adenoma, presenting with **amenorrhoea** (missed periods), **galactorrhoea** (milk discharge) and infertility in women and with macroadenoma mass effects like headache and visual field cuts in men who present later with larger tumours.

vis.alt: Sellar diagram with prolactinoma, optic chiasm, pituitary stalk and cavernous sinuses.
vis.caption: Prolactinoma sellar anatomy with chiasm, stalk and sinuses. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.say: Mild hormone rises mislead. Only high values with a visible lump confirm a true prolactinoma.
steps.tx: **Stalk compression hyperprolactinemia** (squeeze raised milk hormone) stays below **100 to 200 ng per mL** (one to two hundred units), so higher values with a macroadenoma confirm true prolactinoma while modest rises need other causes like drugs, hypothyroidism and kidney failure excluded first.

steps.say: Tablets shrink most of these tumours. Surgery waits for resistance, intolerance or cysts that drugs cannot drain.
steps.tx: **Cabergoline** (milk hormone blocker) is first-line and shrinks most **macroprolactinomas** (large milk lumps), with surgery reserved for drug resistance, intolerance, cystic components or visual compression unresponsive to **dopamine agonists** (brain chemical mimics) after adequate trials, with echocardiography for valvulopathy on high cumulative doses.

steps.say: Shrinking tumours can spring a leak. New watery nasal discharge on tablets is an emergency, not a side effect to watch.
steps.tx: Rapid tumour shrinkage on cabergoline can open a **CSF leak** (brain water nose leak) through **skull base erosion** (eaten bone gap), so new **rhinorrhoea** (watery nose flow) on treatment needs urgent skull base assessment with beta transferrin testing rather than simple drug stoppage at home.

steps.say: Sudden worst headache with double vision and collapse means the lump bled. Steroids come before scans and surgeons.
steps.tx: **Pituitary apoplexy** (lump stroke) presents with sudden headache, **ophthalmoplegia** (eye movement loss), visual loss and **adrenal crisis** (cortisol collapse) from haemorrhage into an adenoma, often precipitated by anticoagulation, surgery or dynamic testing in unsuspected lumps, with third nerve involvement localising cavernous sinus invasion.

vis.alt: Sagittal MRI of sellar mass with apoplexy blood signal.
vis.caption: Pituitary apoplexy with sellar mass blood signal on MRI. Credit: Dr. Frank Gaillard via Wikimedia Commons.

steps.say: Cortisol first, chisel second. Replacement saves life within minutes while decompression waits for visual decline.
steps.tx: Immediate high-dose **hydrocortisone** (stress steroid) precedes all decisions in apoplexy, and urgent **transsphenoidal decompression** (nose route pressure relief) follows **visual deterioration** (worsening sight) of acuity or fields, with stable vision watched on steroids and serial charting, plus cortisol day curves guiding replacement tapering.

steps.say: Small silent lumps are watched, not drilled. Hormones and vision decide, not size alone.
steps.tx: **Pituitary incidentalomas** (chance found lumps) below **10 mm** (one centimetre) with normal hormones and vision are watched with MRI, while larger lesions get full pituitary panel plus formal **visual fields** (side vision test) and stalk effect assessment at baseline, with pregnancy prompting symptom review each trimester.

steps.say: Not every cyst is a tumour. A quiet developmental cyst without calcium simply needs watching.
steps.tx: **Rathke cleft cysts** (leftover pouch cysts) are non-enhancing intrasellar cysts without calcification that mimic adenoma, and asymptomatic ones are observed while compressive ones with visual or hormonal loss are drained **transsphenoidally** (through nose route) with wall biopsy, with diabetes insipidus flagging stalk involvement preoperatively.
